I hope it doesn't get too hot, don’t you?
Yes, I prefer cooler weather.
How old are you?
I am 14 years old.
Where are you heading?
I'm going to the grocery store.
Do you know the price of this?
Yes, it's $15.
What is your name?
My name is Sarah Wilson.
Would you like a lift to the library?
No, thanks, I prefer to walk.
How do I get to the train station?
Walk straight for three blocks, then turn left.
Have you read that book?
No, but I heard it’s really interesting.
What’s your favorite food?
I love pizza.
Is your mother at home?
Yes, just a second, I'll get her for you.
Can I help you?
Yes, I am looking for the electronics section.

title: Sea Animals
sentences: Many people are interested in sea animals.
Some sea animals can be dangerous, like sharks.
Some sea animals, such as jellyfish, have a painful sting.
Other sea animals are friendly.
Dolphins are very smart.
Dolphins use sounds to talk to each other.
Turtles swim in the ocean.
Some turtles can live for more than 100 years.
Crabs have hard shells and big claws.
Some crabs walk sideways on the beach.
Octopuses have eight arms.
They can change color to hide.
Seahorses are very special fish.
The father seahorse carries the babies.
Starfish have five arms and can grow new ones.
Stingrays are flat and swim smoothly.
They hide under the sand.
Jellyfish float in the ocean.
Some jellyfish glow in the dark.
Clownfish live in sea anemones.
Whales are the biggest sea animals.
Some whales sing songs under the water.
Sea otters use rocks to break shells.
They hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift away.
Many sea animals help keep the ocean clean.
It is important to take care of the ocean.
Have you ever seen any of these sea animals?

title: The Bathroom
sentences: The bathroom is where we wash and get ready for the day.
There is a bathtub in the bathroom.
You can fill the bathtub with warm water to take a bath.
There is a shower in the bathroom.
We turn on the shower to wash ourselves.
There is a sink in the bathroom.
We use the sink to wash our hands and face.
There is a mirror above the sink.
We look in the mirror when we brush our hair.
The bathroom has a toilet.
We flush the toilet after we use it.
We keep toilet paper beside the toilet.
There is a cabinet in the bathroom.
We store towels, soap, and shampoo in the cabinet.
There is a towel rack on the wall.
We hang our towels on the towel rack.
There is a bath mat on the floor.
The bath mat keeps the floor dry when we step out of the shower.
We have a toothbrush and toothpaste in the bathroom.
We brush our teeth every morning and night.
There is a hairdryer in the bathroom.
We use the hairdryer to dry our hair after a shower.
We have a soap dispenser near the sink.
There is also a laundry basket in the bathroom.
We put our dirty clothes in the laundry basket.
Some bathrooms have a small window for fresh air.
The bathroom is where we keep ourselves clean and fresh.

title: What You See in a Department Store
sentences: What do you see when you go to a department store?
The aisles are filled with many different products.
There are also shelves and display cases filled with items.
There are sometimes sales tables in the middle of the aisles.
There are different sections in the department store.
There is the clothing section.
In the clothing section, you can find shirts, pants, dresses, and jackets.
There are also accessories like scarves, hats, and gloves.
There is the shoe department.
In the shoe department, you can find sneakers, sandals, and boots.
There is also a jewelry section.
You can find rings, necklaces, and bracelets in the jewelry section.
The electronics section has many gadgets.
Here you would find televisions, headphones, and cameras.
There is a home goods section.
This is where you would find kitchenware, towels, and bedding.
There is a toy section for children.
You can find dolls, action figures, and board games there.
There is a beauty and personal care section.
This section has makeup, skincare products, and shampoo.
There is a home improvement section.
You can find tools, light bulbs, and paint in this section.
There is even a pet section.
You can buy pet food, leashes, and pet toys there.
The department store has almost everything you need.

title: Eating at a Restaurant
sentences: When you enter a restaurant, you might see a sign that says,
"Please wait to be seated."
A server will greet you and ask how many people are in your group.
They may ask if you have a reservation.
The server will then guide you to your table.
You might sit at a booth, a regular table, or at the counter.
Once you are seated, the server will give you a menu.
Some restaurants have separate menus for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
There may also be a drink menu and a dessert menu.
The menu lists different dishes along with their prices.
On your table, you will find utensils.
Utensils include knives, forks, and spoons.
There will also be a napkin for you to use.
It is polite to place your napkin on your lap before eating.
Your waiter or waitress will come to take your order.
You might start with an appetizer.
Some people like to have soup or salad before the main course.
After your meal, you may order dessert, coffee, or tea.
If you need anything, you can call the waiter or waitress.
When you are ready to leave, you will ask for the bill.
Some restaurants bring the bill to your table, while others require you to pay at the counter.
It is customary to leave a tip for the server.
After paying, you can leave and enjoy the rest of your day.

title: Road Safety and Traffic Rules
sentences: Cars, buses, and trucks move along the roads and highways.
Drivers must follow traffic rules to keep the roads safe.
Everyone in the car should wear a seatbelt.
Seatbelts help prevent injuries in case of an accident.
Drivers must stop at stop signs.
Traffic lights control the flow of vehicles.
A red light means stop.
A green light means go.
A yellow light means slow down and be ready to stop.
Some streets have school zones.
Drivers must slow down near schools because children may be crossing.
Crosswalks are marked places for pedestrians to cross the street.
Pedestrians have the right of way at crosswalks.
If you hear a siren, you must move to the side of the road.
Emergency vehicles like fire trucks, ambulances, and police cars need to pass quickly.
When a school bus turns on its flashing lights, all cars must stop.
Children may be crossing the road to or from the bus.
It is important to obey speed limits.
Driving too fast can be dangerous.
People should never use their phones while driving.
It is also very dangerous to drive after drinking alcohol.
Drivers must always stay focused on the road.
Following traffic rules helps keep everyone safe.
Good drivers always follow the rules and drive carefully.

title: Work in a school
sentences: Some people work in a school.
There are special tools that teachers and students need to do their work.
There is a blackboard or whiteboard in the classroom.
There is a telephone in the school office.
Most of the time, the school secretary answers the telephone.
The secretary sits at a desk in the school office.
The secretary has pens, markers, and notebooks on the desk.
Some other things that you would find in a school include:
A stapler to staple papers together.
A photocopier to make copies of worksheets.
A pencil sharpener to keep pencils sharp.
A water fountain where students can get a drink of water.
A hole punch to make holes in worksheets for binders.
Erasers to correct mistakes.
Some schools have many classrooms.
All of the teachers have their own desks in the classrooms.
Some schools have a principal and a vice principal in an office.
There are often many important documents in a school.
Important documents can include student records and report cards.
Students often have to fill out forms for school activities.
Some schools have bookshelves filled with textbooks and reference books.
The books contain important information that students need for their studies.
You’ll have to visit a school sometime.
Maybe it will be an elementary school or a high school.
There are many different types of schools.

title: A Day in the Fall
sentences: It gets cooler in the fall.
The leaves on the trees change color.
My favorite fall colors are red, orange, and yellow.
The leaves fall off the trees and cover the ground.
My friends and I like to jump into big piles of leaves.
Sometimes we help rake the leaves into a pile.
I wear a sweater when I go outside.
The wind blows more in the fall.
I can smell the smoke from people burning wood in their fireplaces.
My mom makes warm soup on chilly days.
I like to eat soup with crackers.
On sunny fall days, we go for walks in the park.
We see squirrels gathering acorns.
The birds begin to fly south for the winter.
My dad helps me pick apples from the apple tree.
Sometimes we bake an apple pie.
Fall is the time for harvest.
My school has a fall festival every year.
We play games, eat snacks, and wear cozy clothes.
In the evenings, we like to drink hot chocolate.
Fall is a beautiful and peaceful season.
I love watching the leaves fall and feeling the cool breeze.
Fall is a time to get ready for winter.
But I always enjoy every moment of autumn.

title: Being Polite and Showing Respect
sentences: Being polite shows that you respect other people.
People enjoy being around someone who is kind and well-mannered.
Always remember to say “please” when you ask for something.
For example, you can say, “Could I please have a cookie?”
When someone gives you something, say “thank you.”
A simple thank you can make someone feel appreciated.
Being polite also means not interrupting when others are talking.
You should wait your turn to speak.
If you need to speak, you can say “excuse me.”
It’s not polite to shout or use rude words.
At the table, you should chew with your mouth closed.
You shouldn’t talk with food in your mouth.
You should wait until everyone is served before you start eating.
Don’t grab food from other people’s plates.
When you cough or sneeze, cover your mouth and nose.
Say “bless you” when someone sneezes.
It’s not polite to point at people.
You should always ask before borrowing something.
Don’t take things that aren’t yours.
Good manners also mean helping others when you can.
Hold the door open for someone coming behind you.
Say kind words and give compliments when they are deserved.
Being polite makes the world a nicer place.
If you treat others kindly, they will likely treat you the same way.
Politeness is a habit you can build every day.

title: Everyone Is Unique
sentences: I am unique.
There is no one else exactly like me in the whole world.
Someone might look a little like me, but they are not me.
I have my own ideas, my own voice, and my own feelings.
That makes me special.
Everyone is different in some way.
Some people are tall, and some are short.
Some people have curly hair, and some have straight hair.
Some people are good at sports, and others are good at music or art.
It’s good to be yourself.
You don’t need to be like everyone else.
I try to be kind and fair to others.
I also try to listen and learn new things.
My friend Alex is very different from me.
He has blue eyes and I have brown eyes.
He loves reading books, and I prefer drawing.
He runs fast, and I sing well.
Even though we’re different, we are good friends.
We talk and laugh and help each other.
Sometimes we have different opinions, and that’s okay.
It’s fun to learn from people who are not like you.
If everyone was exactly the same, life would be boring.
Our differences make life interesting and colorful.
I like being me.
I’m proud of who I am.
You are special too, and you have something great to share.
Let’s celebrate what makes each of us different.

title: My Puppy Max
sentences: I got my dog when he was just a little puppy.
I named him Max because he looked brave and strong.
Max has brown fur with a white patch on his chest.
He has floppy ears and a shiny black nose.
He barks whenever someone knocks on the door.
I feed him dry dog food and sometimes give him a bone as a treat.
After eating, he always drinks a lot of water.
He loves our family and follows us around the house.
Max likes to lie at my feet when I do my homework.
He wags his tail when he's happy.
Max is very playful and full of energy.
He chases after balls and squeaky toys.
Sometimes we play tug-of-war with an old towel.
Max also likes running in the yard.
He barks at birds but never tries to catch them.
At night, he curls up on a pillow beside my bed.
I gave him a soft blanket, and he loves it.
When he's sleepy, he yawns and lies down quietly.
Sometimes he dreams and his legs twitch while he sleeps.
I reach down to pet him, and he sighs happily.
Max is my best friend.
I’m so happy he’s part of our family.

title: People in a Family
sentences: A family is made up of different people.
Families can be big or small.
Most families have parents and children.
A father is the dad in the family.
A mother is the mom in the family.
Fathers and mothers take care of their children.
Children can be sons or daughters.
A son is a boy.
A daughter is a girl.
Some families have brothers and sisters.
A brother is a boy in the family.
A sister is a girl in the family.
Grandparents are part of the family too.
A grandfather is your father’s or mother’s dad.
A grandmother is your father’s or mother’s mom.
Aunts and uncles are also family members.
An aunt is your mom or dad’s sister.
An uncle is your mom or dad’s brother.
Cousins are the children of your aunts and uncles.
All of these people are part of your family.
Families love and care for each other.
It’s nice to spend time with your family.
Every family is special in its own way.

title: Saving and Using Money
sentences: I keep my money in a savings account.
I like to save money for things I want to buy.
I started saving coins in a small box.
A cent is the smallest amount of money.
Five cents make a nickel.
Ten cents is a dime.
Twenty-five cents is called a quarter.
Four quarters equal one full dollar.
One dollar is the same as 100 cents.
I saved many one-dollar coins in a jar.
In Canada, one-dollar coins are called loonies.
We also have two-dollar coins called toonies.
There are also paper bills.
We have five-dollar and ten-dollar bills.
If you're lucky, you might have a twenty, fifty, or even a hundred-dollar bill.
Canadian bills come in many different colors.
That makes it easy to tell them apart.
Some people like to use coins.
Other people prefer using cards or cash.
It's smart to save money for the future.
You can use your savings to buy something special or to help in emergencies.
If you save often, your money can grow.
Saving money is a good habit.
One day, you might save enough for something big.

title: A Trip to the Dentist
sentences: I had a toothache last month, and it really hurt.
My dad made an appointment with the dentist.
When we got to the dental office, the receptionist asked for my name.
Then she told me to sit down and wait for the dentist.
The dental office was very clean and smelled like mint.
Soon, the dental assistant called my name.
She took me to a big chair that leaned back.
She put a bib around my neck and told me to relax.
The dentist came in and smiled at me.
He wore gloves, a mask, and glasses.
He used a tiny mirror to look inside my mouth.
He said one of my teeth had a small cavity.
He said he could fix it right away.
I was nervous, but he said it wouldn't take long.
The dentist gave me a little freezing shot.
I felt a tiny pinch, but it didn’t really hurt.
Then he cleaned out the cavity and filled it with a special material.
The whole thing took about twenty minutes.
When he finished, he told me to avoid chewing on that side for a while.
He also reminded me to brush my teeth twice a day.
He said I should come back in six months for a checkup.
I thanked the dentist and the assistant.
My dad gave me a thumbs up when I came out.
I felt proud of myself for being brave.
I think going to the dentist isn’t so bad after all!

title: My First Job
sentences: I just started working at the public library.
This is my very first job.
I will get paid every two weeks.
I wear a name tag that shows I work at the library.
I have many tasks to do at the library.
I help return books to the correct shelves.
I organize books by author’s last name and by category.
This morning, I shelved storybooks, science books, and cookbooks.
I also help clean tables and reading areas.
I check to make sure chairs are pushed in and magazines are neat.
Sometimes I help people find books.
This morning, a man asked me where the history books were.
I also showed a little girl where the picture books were.
I like helping people.
I also help check books back in using the computer system.
The librarian is teaching me how to check books out too.
Sometimes I put up displays for new books.
I enjoy making signs and arranging the books so they look nice.
I would like to work at the front desk someday.
I think it would be fun to check books out for people.
Or maybe, I could read stories during children’s hour.
I like working at the library.
I hope I can work part-time here even after school starts.

title: My School Library
sentences: My school library is a quiet and cozy place.
It has shelves full of books from the floor to the ceiling.
The books are arranged neatly by topics and authors.
There are storybooks, picture books, and books full of facts.
I like to sit on the soft carpet and read quietly.
There are small tables and chairs where we can do our work.
Sometimes our teacher brings us here for reading time.
The librarian is very friendly and helps us find books.
We each have a library card so we can borrow books.
I always borrow books about animals and space.
There’s a quiet corner with beanbag chairs.
That’s where we sit to read when we don’t have class.
On the wall, there are posters that say “Read Every Day.”
There’s also a big clock so we don’t forget the time.
Every Friday, we have library time with our class.
We each return our books and borrow new ones.
Sometimes we read aloud to our reading buddies.
During holidays, the library has fun contests and events.
I once won a bookmark for reading the most books in a month.
I like being in the library because it’s peaceful.
After library time, my friends and I talk about our favorite books.
We recommend stories to each other and plan what to read next.
The library is one of my favorite places in school.

title: A Visit to the New Baby
sentences: My cousin just had a baby boy.
We went to the hospital to visit her and see the new baby.
My cousin was feeling fine, though she was a little tired.
She took us to a room with a big window that had a lot of babies in it.
She pointed to a crib with a little baby boy inside.
The baby was wrapped in a light blue blanket.
We all said how cute the baby looked.
I couldn't believe how small the baby was.
The baby was asleep, so we couldn__ see his eyes.
After the baby went home, we went to visit him.
We heard the baby crying from inside.
My cousin said the baby was hungry.
She had a baby bottle with warm milk.
She fed the baby with the bottle.
After feeding, the baby was happy and stopped crying.
My cousin gently patted the baby on his back until he burped.
Then, the baby fell back to sleep.
I held the baby in my arms.
I looked at his tiny hands and tiny feet.
I was very careful with him, not to wake him up.
The baby opened his eyes and looked up at me.
I spoke softly to the baby, even though I knew he couldn't understand me.
Babies have to learn how to walk and talk.
My cousin changed the baby__ diaper.
Babies wear diapers, so they need to be changed often.
The baby already has many toys, but he is still too young to play with them.
My cousin says it won__ be long before the baby is crawling and starting to talk.
Babies are so cute.

title: Different Hobbies
sentences: Many people have hobbies they enjoy doing in their free time.
Hobbies are fun, and they help people relax.
My older sister’s hobby is baking.
She makes cupcakes, cookies, and even her own bread.
She decorates her cakes with icing and sprinkles.
My grandfather loves gardening.
He grows vegetables like tomatoes, carrots, and lettuce.
He also has flowers that bloom in the spring and summer.
My friend Kevin’s hobby is building things with wood.
He has built a birdhouse and a small bookshelf.
My cousin loves photography.
He takes pictures of animals, trees, and sunsets.
He uses a big camera with different lenses.
My classmate Emily likes to write stories.
She keeps a notebook full of her ideas.
She wants to write a book one day.
My neighbor’s hobby is knitting.
She makes scarves, hats, and mittens for her family.
My dad enjoys playing the guitar.
He plays music on weekends and sings songs too.
Some hobbies are quiet, and some are active.
Some people read books, while others go hiking or skateboarding.
All hobbies are special in their own way.
A hobby can be just for fun, or it can turn into something big.
I think hobbies are a great way to learn and grow.

title: Graduation Day
sentences: The sound of the school bell rings through the air.
I am inside the auditorium, waiting for my cousin to walk across the stage.
Today is her graduation day.
She is wearing a cap and gown, and she looks so proud.
The principal is standing at the front, welcoming the students and their families.
The crowd rises as my cousin's name is called.
She walks across the stage with a smile, shaking hands with the principal.
She is handed her diploma, and we all clap.
The ceremony continues with more students, each receiving their diploma.
After the ceremony, we take pictures with the graduate.
My cousin looks so happy and excited for the future.
We all gather for a family celebration at a restaurant.
We share a meal and talk about all the wonderful things she will do in the future.
Some of us give speeches, and everyone is proud of what she has accomplished.
The photographer captures many joyful moments of the celebration.
After dinner, we play games and dance to celebrate her success.
My cousin throws a graduation hat into the air, and everyone cheers.
The next day, she will leave for a vacation with her friends.
My cousin and her friends are going to the beach for a fun and relaxing time.

title: About Opposites
sentences: Opposites help us understand the world better.
The opposite of full is empty.
The opposite of noisy is quiet.
When something is hard, the opposite is soft.
The opposite of early is late.
If something is light, its opposite is heavy.
If something is smooth, the opposite is rough.
The opposite of open is closed.
A clean shirt is the opposite of a dirty one.
A straight line is the opposite of a curved one.
A narrow road is the opposite of a wide one.
A sharp knife is the opposite of a dull knife.
The opposite of fast is slow.
The opposite of high is low.
The opposite of outside is inside.
If I’m sitting, the opposite is standing.
If I’m awake,
the opposite is asleep.
If I say “go,” the opposite is “stop.”
If the answer is yes, then the opposite is no.
You can walk forwards or backwards—those are opposites too.
Something new is the opposite of something old.
Wet and dry are opposites we often notice after it rains.
You feel awake in the day, and sleepy at night—those are opposites.
Let’s play a game: I say one word, and you say its opposite!
Opposites are everywhere—can you find more around you?

title: Different Places People Live
sentences: I live in a small apartment with my family.
Our apartment is on the third floor.
My teacher lives in a townhouse with her husband.
My friend Jake lives in a high-rise building in the city.
My cousin lives on a boat.
He and his parents sail from one port to another.
My grandparents live in a bungalow near the beach.
My neighbor is a student.
She lives in a shared house with four other people.
My pen pal in Japan lives in a house with sliding paper doors.
My uncle is a soldier.
He lives in army barracks.
When we go camping, we live in a cabin in the woods.
My older brother is traveling the world.
Right now, he’s staying in a youth hostel in Germany.
Some people live in houseboats on rivers.
In very cold places, some people used to live in igloos made of snow.
In hot deserts, some people live in tents made of fabric.
Some families live in huts made of mud and sticks.
People live in many different types of homes around the world.
I sometimes imagine what it would be like to live in a treehouse.
Or maybe even a space station one day!

title: I Live Near Yellowstone National Park
sentences: I live near Yellowstone National Park.
Yellowstone is a famous place.
A lot of tourists visit here every year.
Most of the tourists come to see the geysers and wildlife.
The geysers are amazing, especially Old Faithful.
It shoots hot water high into the air like a fountain.
People stand nearby and wait for the geyser to erupt.
There are also beautiful hot springs with colorful water.
Tourists take pictures of the scenery and the animals.
Sometimes they see bears, elk, or bison.
There are gift shops and campsites in the park.
There are also lodges and hotels for visitors.
Tourism is very important to the people who live nearby.
Many people work as guides, rangers, or shop workers.
You can hike on trails or join a nature tour.
In the winter, people come for cross-country skiing and snowshoeing.
Yellowstone is busiest in the summer.
Families travel from all over the country to visit.
There are stories and legends about the land and animals.
Native American tribes have told stories about Yellowstone for generations.
Some stories explain how the hot springs were formed.
Rangers also share facts and fun tales during park talks.
I’ve visited many parts of the park with my family.
I always stay on the trails and never get too close to the animals.
Yellowstone is full of wonder and stories.
I feel lucky to live so close to such an amazing place.

title: A Lesson About Telling the Truth
sentences: Yesterday, I told a lie.
I didn’t feel good about it.
I was playing with a ball in the kitchen.
The ball hit a cup and broke it.
It was one of my mom’s favorite cups.
I was afraid she would be angry.
I put the broken cup on the table and didn’t say anything.
That night, my mom asked who broke the cup.
My brother said, “Not me.”
My sister said, “I didn’t do it.”
I also said, “It wasn’t me,” but I was not telling the truth.
Mom said we would all be punished if no one told the truth.
She gave us another chance and said she wouldn’t be angry.
She just wanted us to be honest.
I still didn’t say anything.
So, my brother, sister and I were sent to our rooms.
We had to stay there all morning.
My brother said it wasn’t fair.
I felt very bad because they were punished because of me.
Then I went to my mom and told her the truth.
I said I was the one who broke the cup.
She said she was not mad about the cup.
She said she was upset because I didn’t tell the truth.
She said she wouldn’t have punished me if I had been honest.
I told my brother and sister that I was sorry.
I also told my mom that I was sorry for lying.
I learned an important lesson.
It is always better to tell the truth.
Lying only makes things worse.
People won’t trust you if you lie.
I want to be someone that others can trust.

title: About Emotions
sentences: Do you ever think about how you feel?
What makes you feel sad?
I feel sad when I get a bad grade at school.
I also feel sad when someone I like moves away.
Sometimes I watch sad movies that make me cry.
I don’t like feeling sad.
I like feeling happy.
I am happy most of the time.
I feel happy when I go to a party.
Being with my friends also makes me happy.
I laugh when someone tells a funny joke.
I think smiling makes people look nice.
What makes you angry?
I get angry when my brother breaks my toy.
I try not to yell when I’m angry.
My parents get angry if I come home late.
I think it’s better to stay calm and talk.
Our feelings come from inside,
but other people can see them on our face.
People know when we are sad, happy, or mad.
I try to smile even when I feel sad.
Smiling helps me feel a little better.

title: Going to a Restaurant
sentences: When you go to a restaurant, you might see a sign that says,
"Please wait to be seated."
A host or hostess will ask how many people are with you.
Then they will ask if you want to sit in the smoking or non-smoking area.
They will take you to your seat.
You may sit at a table or in a booth.
You will get a menu to look at.
Sometimes there are different menus for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
There might also be a menu for drinks and desserts.
The food and prices are listed on the menu.
On the table, there are knives, forks, and spoons.
These are called cutlery.
There is also a napkin on the table.
You should put the napkin on your lap when you eat.
A waiter or waitress will come and take your order.
You might want to start with a salad or soup.
After your meal, you can have a dessert, tea, or coffee.
When you are finished, you will pay the bill.

title: Housework at Home
sentences: When you live in a house, there is always something to do.
You have to clean the windows so you can see outside.
The floors and carpets need to be vacuumed often.
Some floors also need to be washed and waxed.
The furniture needs to be dusted and polished.
The bathroom must be kept clean.
After taking a bath, clean the bathtub.
Laundry must be done regularly.
You put dirty clothes in the washing machine.
Then, you dry the clothes in the dryer or hang them outside.
Some clothes also need ironing.
You have to shop for groceries and put them away.
You also need to cook meals for the family.
Don’t let the dishes pile up. Wash them after each meal.
Wipe the kitchen counters after cooking.
Sometimes, clean the stove, fridge, and cupboards.
You can also sweep the floor and make the beds.
Change the bed sheets and put on clean ones.
There are always many things to do in a house.
Housework takes time and effort, but it helps keep your home nice and clean.

title: International Students
sentences: There are many international students at my school.
Some of them come from Australia.
They speak English, but their accent is different from a Canadian accent.
Many students come from Brazil.
They are learning our language and culture.
We also have students from Spain, Vietnam, Thailand, Egypt, and Turkey.
We try to help them feel welcome here.
The students enjoy seeing new places.
They go sightseeing and visit tourist spots.
Niagara Falls and Toronto are popular places to visit.
The students practice English by talking to Canadians.
When they arrive, we show them around the school and the city.
They do many exercises to learn English.
They listen to English songs and read English storybooks.
They also listen to English audio recordings.
The best way to learn English is to speak it often.
It is good to ask questions in English.
Canadians try to help international students.
Some students live with host families.
Living with a host family helps them learn about Canadian life.
The students eat Canadian food and follow Canadian routines.
Many students stay in touch with their host families after they go home.

title: Playing an Instrument
sentences: If you were in an orchestra, what instrument would you play?
Would you like to play a big tuba, a trumpet, or a saxophone?
Maybe you prefer string instruments like the violin or cello.
Some people like to play percussion instruments.
You can play the drums or the cymbals.
Some instruments have keyboards.
A piano and an organ both have keyboards.
Guitars, banjos, and mandolins are stringed instruments.
Some instruments need air to make sound.
You blow into a flute, a French horn, or a harmonica.
In an orchestra, everyone watches the conductor.
The conductor tells the players when to start and stop.
You can also join a band just for fun.
Some people join a rock band or a dance band.
People who play music often learn how to read notes.
Notes are written on lines called a staff.
There are different kinds of notes like whole notes and quarter notes.
Each note lasts for a different number of beats.
If you want to learn an instrument, music lessons are helpful.
Learning music can be fun and a good skill to have.

title: A Trip in My Imagination
sentences: I like to pretend.
I like to make up things that are not real.
I use my imagination.
Yesterday, I pretended I had a time machine.
I set the machine to go back to the time of the dinosaurs.
The machine made loud noises and spun very fast.
Then, it stopped.
I opened the door and stepped outside.
I was in a jungle.
The trees were tall and the plants were thick.
I could hear strange animal sounds.
I saw a big bird with a long beak fly above me.
I walked a little, but I stayed close to my time machine.
Suddenly, I saw a man.
He looked very different.
He wore animal skin and held a big stick.
He made some sounds I didn’t understand.
Then the ground started to shake.
I heard loud thumping noises.
A huge dinosaur came through the trees.
The man ran away.
The dinosaur was coming toward me!
My heart was beating fast.
I ran back to my time machine.
I set it to go home to the 21st century.
The machine spun and buzzed again.
I landed back in my time.
I was safe.
I love using my imagination!

title: I Want to Wear Different Clothes
sentences: My friends at school wear many different types of clothes.
Some of them like baggy jeans and big T-shirts.
Others wear very colorful clothes with fun patterns.
My best friend Lily wears black clothes and lots of jewelry.
I told my parents that I want to try a new style too.
I saw a cool jacket with metal buttons and wanted to buy it.
My dad said it looked strange and asked why I wanted it.
I said I wanted to show my personality.
My mom said that clothes should be comfortable and neat.
I said everyone at school is wearing fun clothes.
My mom said, "If everyone wore pajamas to school, would you do it too?"
I laughed and said no.
I asked if I could buy a pair of shoes with flames on them.
My dad said, "Maybe next time."
My mom said when I__ older and have my own money,
I can wear anything I like.
For now, I wear simple clothes, but I still try to be creative.
I add a fun hat or a bright scarf.
Styles change fast.
Maybe next year, everyone will wear something new again.
But I__l always try to wear something that feels like me.

title: Imagine If You Could Fly
sentences: Imagine what life would be like if you could fly like a bird.
You wouldn’t need a car or a bicycle.
You could fly to school every day.
You could go up high into the sky and look down at your house.
Clouds would float beside you, and the wind would blow through your hair.
If you wanted to visit your friend, you could fly right to their window.
If you saw a traffic jam, you would just fly over it.
You could go to the top of a mountain without climbing.
A trip to the beach would be easy and fun.
But flying might not always be safe.
You would have to watch out for airplanes and tall buildings.
You might get tired from flying too long.
Bad weather would make flying hard.
Birds might not like to share the sky with you.
Still, it would be fun to fly above the trees and feel so free.
You could take pictures from the sky and see the world in a new way.
If I could fly, I would visit places I’ve never been to.
I would help people by flying to get things quickly.
At the end of the day, I’d fly home and rest on my roof.
Flying would be amazing, but for now, I’ll just keep dreaming.

title: The Paperboy and the Old Man
sentences: In my town, there is a paperboy who got a special award.
He brings newspapers to people every morning.
One man he gave the newspaper to was very old.
The old man lived alone.
The paperboy talked to him many times.
He always put the newspaper in the man’s mailbox.
One morning, the boy saw that yesterday’s mail and paper were still there.
He thought something might be wrong.
At school, he kept thinking about the old man.
After school, he went back to the old man’s house.
The mail and newspaper were still in the mailbox.
He knocked on the door.
He heard a soft voice but couldn’t understand it.
He tried to open the door, but it was locked.
He ran home and called the police.
He told the police that the old man lived alone.
He gave them the man’s address.
The police came and also heard the soft voice.
They got inside the house.
They found the old man at the bottom of the stairs.
He had fallen and broken his hip.
He could not get up.
He was scared that no one would find him.
The old man was very thankful to the boy.
The boy got an award.
The old man said he was a hero.
The police said he was a great citizen.
Now, the paperboy and the man are good friends.
The man will never forget what the boy did.

title: When Parents Get Divorced
sentences: Emma's parents are getting a divorce.
She feels very sad and confused.
She wonders if it's her fault.
Emma thinks maybe her parents don't love her anymore.
But that is not true.
Her parents still love her very much.
Sometimes, parents can't stay married even if they love their children.
People change as they grow, and sometimes couples grow apart.
Divorce is not the child’s fault.
Children don't cause a divorce, and they can't stop it either.
Emma can still see both of her parents.
She might live with one parent and visit the other.
Her life will be different, but it can still be good.
Some children get stepmothers or stepfathers after a divorce.
That can be hard at first, but it might turn out well.
It is important to talk to someone when you feel sad or confused.
Emma can talk to her mom, her dad, or a teacher or friend.
Divorce is a big change for everyone in the family.
But over time, things usually get better.
Emma knows now that her parents love her no matter what.

title: Avoid Catching a Cold
sentences: Many people get colds several times a year.
When they have a cold, they sneeze and cough a lot.
Their noses run, and their throats feel sore.
Some people always carry tissues with them.
I don't get colds very often.
Sometimes, I can go a whole year without getting sick.
I think I know some good ways to stay healthy.
First, I eat a lot of fruit and vegetables.
I drink orange juice almost every day.
I also take vitamin C tablets.
If I start to feel sick, I take extra vitamin C and rest.
I try to get fresh air every day.
In winter, the air inside buildings is not fresh.
So I go outside for a walk whenever I can.
I also stay away from people who are coughing or sneezing.
If someone sneezes near me, I try not to breathe in for a few seconds.
I always wash my hands after touching things in public places.
Things like doorknobs, handrails and money have lots of germs.
Some people even put money in their mouths. That’s not clean!
I believe eating well, washing hands, and getting rest helps me stay healthy.
If I do catch a cold, I drink a lot of water and get plenty of sleep.
Taking care of yourself is the best way to fight a cold.

title: Getting My Glasses
sentences: Lately, I have had trouble seeing things at school.
The words on the blackboard look blurry.
I also started getting headaches every day.
I told my mother about my problem.
She made an appointment for me to see an eye doctor.
The doctor is called an optometrist.
At the clinic, I looked at a chart with letters on it.
Some letters were big, and some were very small.
The optometrist covered one of my eyes, and asked me to read the letters.
Then she covered the other eye and did the same thing.
She also put some drops in my eyes to check them.
I asked her if I passed the test.
She smiled and said, "This is not a test you pass or fail. We’re just checking your vision."
She told me I needed glasses to help me see better.
My mom and I looked at many different frames.
Some frames looked too big, and some looked too small.
I tried on many pairs and chose one I really liked.
A lady measured my face and said the glasses would be ready on Friday.
On Friday, I picked up my glasses.
I wore them and everything looked so clear!
I went to school with my glasses on Monday.
My classmates said I looked smart in glasses.
Now I can see the blackboard clearly and I don’t get headaches anymore.
I’m really happy that I got glasses.

title: Life in Space
sentences: I sometimes think about what it would be like to live in space.
In the future, people might live on the Moon or even on Mars.
We would have to wear space suits when we go outside.
There is no air on the Moon or Mars, so we would need special helmets to breathe.
Houses in space would be very different.
They might be built under the ground or inside a dome.
We would eat dried food or food made by machines.
We would drink water that is cleaned and used again.
Students would still go to school, but maybe all classes would be online.
Robots might be our helpers in space.
They could help clean, cook, or even fix machines.
Traveling in space would be very exciting.
We could float around in zero gravity.
But living in space might also be hard.
We would miss the trees, the blue sky, and fresh air.
Still, it would be amazing to explore a new world.
Maybe one day, people will really live in space.

title: My Favorite Stuffed Bear
sentences: When I was a little child, I had a stuffed bear.
His name was Benny.
He was brown and soft, and he wore a red ribbon around his neck.
I took Benny everywhere with me.
I took him to the park, to the grocery store, and even to visit my grandparents.
At night, I could not fall asleep without him.
I held him close and told him about my day.
Sometimes, I imagined that he could talk to me.
I told him my secrets, and he always “listened” without saying a word.
One day, I lost Benny at the park.
I cried and cried. I felt like I had lost my best friend.
My dad took me back to the park to look for him.
We found him sitting under a bench, dirty but safe.
I was so happy and hugged him tightly.
As I got older, I didn’t play with Benny as much.
But I never put him away. He always stayed on my bed.
Now, Benny is old and worn out.
His ribbon is faded, and one of his ears is loose.
But I still love him, and I will always keep him.
He reminds me of my childhood and all the good memories I had.

title: My First Music Performance
sentences: Last month, I played the piano at my school concert.
It was the first time I performed music in front of a large audience.
There were about 200 people in the audience, including my parents and teachers.
Before going on stage, I felt very nervous.
My hands were shaking a little, and my heart was beating fast.
I had practiced the song many times at home.
I knew the song very well, but I still felt a little afraid.
When it was my turn, I walked slowly to the piano.
I took a deep breath and began to play.
At first, I made a small mistake, but I didn’t stop.
I just kept going and focused on the music.
After a minute, I forgot about the audience.
I started to enjoy the song and the sound of the piano.
When I finished, people clapped and smiled at me.
I felt very proud of myself.
My music teacher said I did a great job.
Now I know that performing is not as scary as I thought.
I want to play again at the next concert.
Practice and courage helped me enjoy my first performance.
I learned that trying something new can be exciting and fun.

title: My First Trip Abroad
sentences: Last year, I went on my first trip to another country.
I visited France with my family during the summer vacation.
I was very excited before the trip, but I was also a little nervous.
I had never been on an airplane before, so everything felt new to me.
When we arrived in Paris, I noticed that many things were different.
People spoke a different language, and the streets looked unfamiliar.
I didn’t understand any French at first, so it was hard to order food.
I had to use hand gestures and point to pictures on the menu.
The food was very different from what I usually eat.
I tried some new dishes, like escargot and French cheese.
At first I didn’t like everything, but I wanted to keep an open mind.
I also had to get used to how people behave in France.
For example, people greet each other by kissing on both cheeks.
That was very different from what I was used to in my country.
I tried my best to be polite and follow the local customs.
I learned a few simple French phrases, and people were happy when I used them.
After a few days, I started to feel more comfortable.
I enjoyed walking through the city and visiting famous places like the Eiffel Tower.
Traveling to another country helped me understand a new culture.
I would love to visit more countries in the future and learn about the world.

title: What Will You Be in the Future
sentences: Have you ever thought about what you want to be when you grow up?
There are so many jobs to choose from.
Some people want to be police officers.
Others want to become teachers and help students learn.
If you like helping people, you can be a nurse or a doctor.
Doctors take care of sick people, and nurses help them.
Some people want to be cooks or bakers.
They enjoy making food and sharing it with others.
Maybe you love animals.
You could be a veterinarian and help sick animals get better.
If you like music, you might become a singer or a musician.
Some people enjoy acting, so they want to be actors in movies or on stage.
If you are good with your hands, you could be a builder or a mechanic.
You could fix cars or build houses.
Some people want to work in stores.
They might be cashiers or sell clothes and food.
If you like reading, maybe you would enjoy working in a library.
Some people want to be artists or writers.
They use their imagination to create pictures and stories.
There are so many jobs in the world.
You just need to find something you enjoy doing.
If you work hard and believe in yourself, you can be anything you want.

title: If I Could Fly
sentences: Sometimes I imagine what life would be like if I could fly.
I wouldn't need a car or a bus to get around.
I could fly above the traffic and get anywhere very quickly.
I would wake up in the morning, eat breakfast, and fly to school.
All my friends would watch me land in the schoolyard.
I could visit different cities in one day.
I might fly to the beach for lunch and be back by dinner.
I would feel the wind on my face and see everything from above.
But I would have to be careful of birds, airplanes, and bad weather.
If it rained, I would get all wet unless I had a special flying coat.
Flying at night might be fun, but I would need something to help me see in the dark.
I would have to be careful not to scare people below me.
They might not believe their eyes if they saw someone flying!
Maybe I would need a license to fly, just like a pilot.
I could help people by flying up to rescue cats from trees.
I could deliver things to people who need them.
I think flying would be exciting and useful.
But maybe I would miss walking on the ground.
Flying might be tiring if I had to do it all the time.
I think I like being able to walk, run, and sometimes dream about flying.
Maybe it’s best to just fly in my imagination.

title: Staying Healthy
sentences: Being healthy is very important in life.
You can have a good job, a nice house, and lots of money,
but if you are not healthy, you won’t enjoy those things.
Health means feeling good in your body and in your mind.
One way to stay healthy is to get enough sleep.
Sleep helps your body rest and repair itself.
Another way is to eat healthy food.
We need to eat fruits, vegetables, meat, dairy, and grains.
We should not eat too many sweet or oily foods.
Drinking water is also important.
Water helps your body stay cool and clean inside.
Exercise is another key to good health.
It keeps your heart, lungs, and muscles strong.
Exercise also helps your brain work better.
When we do the right things, we feel better inside.
Being kind and helpful to others makes us feel happy.
It also helps us stay calm and less stressed.
Stress is not good for your health.
So we should try to relax and enjoy life.
If we take care of our body and mind,
we can live a happy and healthy life.
Let’s all try our best to stay healthy and help others stay healthy too!

title: Superstitions
sentences: I don’t really believe in superstitions, but I know many people who do.
Yesterday was Friday the 13th, and some people think it’s a very unlucky day.
To me, it was just a normal day like any other.
Some people believe that if a black cat crosses your path, you will have bad luck.
I have seen black cats many times, and nothing bad ever happened to me.
My grandmother says you should never open an umbrella inside the house.
She thinks that will bring bad luck.
Maybe she’s right—if you open an umbrella inside, you could break something!
Some people say that if your left hand is itchy, you will get money.
I’ve had an itchy hand before, but no money came to me!
It is also bad luck to walk under a ladder.
That one makes sense to me. You could get hurt or knock something over.
Actors have their own special superstitions.
They don’t like it when someone says “Good luck” before a performance.
Instead, they say “Break a leg.”
That sounds strange, but it actually means “Good luck.”
I did a school project about superstitions last year.
I learned that many superstitions come from very old stories.
People passed them down from generation to generation.
Some people still believe in them, but others just find them fun to talk about.
I don’t believe in bad luck or magic signs, but I enjoy learning about them.

title: Visiting My Grandpa's Old Farm
sentences: Last summer, I went to the countryside with my dad.
He grew up on a farm, and he wanted to show me the place where he used to live.
We drove for many hours to get there.
The farm was very quiet and peaceful.
There were fields of corn and wheat, and a red barn beside the house.
My grandpa doesn’t live there anymore, but some neighbors still remembered him.
They talked to my dad and laughed about old stories.
One of the neighbors let us ride his horse.
I had never ridden a horse before.
At first, I was scared, but the man helped me get on slowly.
The horse walked slowly, and I held the reins tightly.
My dad laughed and said I looked just like him when he was young.
After the ride, we helped the neighbor feed the chickens.
I had never done anything like that in the city.
My dad showed me how to collect eggs from the chicken coop.
He moved so fast, but I was slow and careful.
I dropped one egg, and it broke on the ground.
The neighbor just smiled and said, “That’s okay. It happens.”
Before we left, my dad and I took a photo in front of the old barn.
It was a special day for both of us.
I learned a lot about what my dad's childhood was like.
Even though the farm was very different from my life now, I really enjoyed the visit.
Maybe one day I will bring my child to see the farm too.

title: A Scary Night Alone
sentences: Last weekend, my parents went to visit my aunt.
I stayed at home alone because I had homework to finish.
At first, everything was quiet and peaceful.
I sat on the sofa and started to watch a mystery movie.
Outside, the sky turned dark, and heavy rain began to fall.
Suddenly, I heard a loud crash of thunder.
The lights in the house flickered and then went out.
I was alone in the dark, and I started to feel scared.
I lit a candle and walked slowly through the house.
Suddenly, I heard a strange tapping sound.
It sounded like someone was knocking on the window.
I held the candle close and walked to the window.
I was shaking a little, but I wanted to see what it was.
I slowly pulled back the curtain.
It was just a tree branch moving in the wind.
I laughed at myself, but I was still nervous.
Then I heard another sound coming from the kitchen.
This time, it sounded like something had fallen.
I walked into the kitchen and looked around.
I saw a spoon on the floor—it must have fallen off the counter.
I realized that I was letting my imagination scare me.
I turned on my flashlight and went back to the sofa.
I waited for the rain to stop and read a book instead.
The rest of the night was quiet.
I learned that being alone in the dark can feel scary,
but most of the time, there’s nothing to be afraid of.

title: Alexander Graham Bell
sentences: Alexander Graham Bell was a famous inventor.
He is best known for inventing the telephone.
Bell was born in Scotland in 1847, the same year as Thomas Edison.
When he was a child, Bell loved learning about sounds and speech.
His father was a teacher who helped people speak clearly.
Bell’s mother was almost deaf, so Bell learned to speak very clearly so she could understand him.
As a young man, Bell moved to Canada and then to the United States.
He started teaching deaf students how to speak.
Bell was very interested in how people hear and speak.
He began to study machines that could carry sound through wires.
Bell worked with another man named Thomas Watson.
Together, they built a machine that could send voices from one place to another.
In 1876, Bell spoke the first words on the telephone.
He said, “Mr. Watson, come here. I want to see you.”
Watson heard the words clearly through the telephone.
This was the beginning of a big change in communication.
Before the telephone, people had to send letters or use the telegraph.
Bell’s invention made it possible to talk to someone far away.
Soon, telephones were used in homes and businesses all over the world.
Bell did not stop inventing after the telephone.
He also worked on other projects, like improving the phonograph and flying machines.
Bell believed in helping people.
He spent time and money helping deaf people learn to speak.
Bell also started a company, which later became known as Bell Telephone.
Alexander Graham Bell died in 1922, but his invention changed the world forever.
Today, we use mobile phones and the internet, but it all started with Bell’s first telephone.
Bell once said, “When one door closes, another opens.”
He believed that people should never stop trying new things.

title: Egypt – Land of the Nile and Ancient Wonders
sentences: Egypt is a country located in North Africa.
It is famous for its ancient history and beautiful landscapes.
The Nile River runs through Egypt and is the longest river in the world.
Most people in Egypt live near the Nile, where the land is good for farming.
The capital city of Egypt is Cairo, one of the largest cities in Africa.
Egypt has a very rich history that goes back thousands of years.
Ancient Egypt is known for its pyramids, temples, and great pharaohs.
The most famous pyramid is the Great Pyramid of Giza.
Nearby is the Sphinx, a giant statue with the body of a lion and the head of a man.
The ancient Egyptians believed in many gods and the afterlife.
They built tombs for their kings called pharaohs and filled them with treasures.
One famous pharaoh is Tutankhamun, whose tomb was found with many golden items.
Today, people from around the world visit Egypt to see these ancient wonders.
Egypt was later ruled by the Greeks, Romans, Arabs, and others.
Arabic is the official language of Egypt today.
Islam is the main religion, and most Egyptians are Muslims.
Egyptian people are known for their hospitality and strong family values.
Egyptian food includes dishes like falafel, koshari, and pita bread.
Tea is a popular drink in Egypt, often served with sugar or mint.
In modern times, Egypt is a mix of old and new.
Many people live in large cities, but some still live in desert villages.
Tourism is very important to Egypt's economy.
People visit museums in Cairo to see mummies, statues, and ancient artifacts.
Some tourists take Nile River cruises to see temples and enjoy the views.
Egyptians celebrate many holidays, including Ramadan and national festivals.
Egyptian music and dance are colorful and full of energy.
Egyptians are proud of their history and hopeful about the future.
Egypt is a land of history, culture, and beauty that continues to inspire the world.

title: Learning to Drive
sentences: Every year, many teenagers and young adults start learning how to drive.
Driving is important because it helps people go to school, work, and other places.
Before you start driving, you should know the basic traffic rules.
There are many road signs that you need to understand.
You should also know when to stop, turn, or change lanes.
It’s also important to learn how to use the car controls.
You need to know how to use the lights, the horn, the brakes, and the steering wheel.
At first, driving can feel difficult.
That’s why people need to practice a lot.
A good place to start is an empty parking lot.
You can practice turning, stopping, and starting in a safe space.
After that, you can try driving on quiet roads.
At the beginning, it’s best to have an experienced driver with you.
Some people take lessons from driving schools.
Driving instructors teach you how to drive safely.
When you are ready, you can take a driving test.
You have to show that you can drive well and follow the rules.
In the test, you may need to park, turn, and drive in traffic.
If you pass the test, you will get your driver’s license.
Even after getting a license, you must drive carefully.
Always follow the rules and be respectful to other drivers.
Safe driving is important for you and for everyone on the road.

title: Listening to the Radio
sentences: When I drive my car, I like to listen to the radio.
The radio lets me enjoy music and hear the news at the same time.
You don’t have to be in a car to enjoy the radio.
Many people listen to the radio at home or at work.
Every city has many different radio stations.
Some radio stations talk about news and world events.
Other stations have talk shows, where people call in to ask questions.
Many radio stations focus on music.
Some stations play the most popular songs right now.
These are often called “Top 100” songs.
Some stations play only one kind of music, like classical or jazz.
Other stations play rock, country, or rhythm and blues.
If you like soft and relaxing music, there are stations for that too.
No matter what kind of music you enjoy, you can find a station that plays it.
Some radio stations also tell stories or read books aloud.
Sometimes you can even hear a whole play on the radio.
Even though we have TV and the Internet, people still enjoy radio.
Radio is an easy way to get information and entertainment.
I think people will continue to listen to the radio for many years.
It’s a fun part of everyday life.

title: Learning Tennis
sentences: Last year I decided to learn how to play tennis.
At the beginning, it was very difficult for me.
I didn’t know how to hold the racket the right way.
I often missed the ball and felt frustrated.
My friend Julia offered to teach me.
She showed me how to stand and how to swing the racket.
At first, I could not hit the ball over the net.
Julia told me to be patient and keep practicing.
After a few weeks, I began to hit the ball better.
I learned how to serve the ball.
Serving was difficult, but I improved slowly.
Playing tennis is also good exercise.
It makes my arms and legs stronger.
Now, I can play short games with my friends.
Sometimes I win, and sometimes I lose.
Winning is fun, but losing helps me learn too.
I enjoy tennis because it keeps me active.
I also like it because I can play with friends.
I hope to become even better at tennis in the future.
Learning tennis taught me that practice is the key.

title: Marie Curie
sentences: Marie Curie was one of the most important scientists of the modern age.
She was born as Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw, Poland, in 1867.
As a young woman, she moved to Paris to study at the Sorbonne.
She studied physics and mathematics and worked very hard.
In Paris, she met the scientist Pierre Curie, and they married.
The two of them became a team in the laboratory.
They began to study a strange kind of energy called radioactivity.
In 1898, they discovered two new elements: polonium and radium.
These elements gave off strong energy that could pass through many materials.
Marie developed careful methods to separate tiny amounts of radium from rock.
Her work helped create new fields in physics and chemistry.
In 1903, Marie and Pierre Curie, with Henri Becquerel, won the Nobel Prize in Physics.
In 1911, Marie Curie won a second Nobel Prize, this time in Chemistry.
She was the first person ever to win two Nobel Prizes.
Her discoveries soon helped doctors treat some cancers with radiation.
During World War I, she organized mobile X-ray units for wounded soldiers.
Many people called these small X-ray cars “Little Curies.”
Marie also trained nurses and drivers to use the machines safely.
At that time, people did not fully understand the dangers of radiation.
Marie often worked without the protection we use today.
Years of exposure damaged her health.
She died in 1934 from a blood illness related to radiation.
Even so, her work changed science and medicine around the world.
She also opened doors for women in science through her courage and success.
Today, research centers named after Curie still help patients and train scientists.
Marie Curie showed that great discoveries come from effort and patience.
She believed in hard work and careful experiments.
Her life continues to inspire students and researchers everywhere.

title: Italian Immigration to the United States
sentences: In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, many people from Italy moved to the United States.
Most of these immigrants came from the southern parts of Italy, where life was very difficult.
Many families were poor, and they hoped for better opportunities in America.
At that time, the United States was growing quickly and needed workers.
Italian immigrants often found jobs in construction, factories, and farms.
Many helped build roads, bridges, and even parts of the New York subway system.
Life was not easy for Italian immigrants.
They often lived in crowded neighborhoods with poor living conditions.
Some Americans did not welcome them and treated them unfairly.
Despite the difficulties, Italians worked hard and supported their families.
Many sent money back to relatives in Italy, just as Chinese workers once did.
Over time, Italian immigrants built strong communities in cities like New York, Boston, and Chicago.
They opened shops, restaurants, and churches, which became centers of their culture.
Italian food, such as pizza and pasta, soon became popular with Americans.
Today, Italian Americans are an important part of U.S. society.
They have made great contributions in politics, business, sports, and the arts.
The story of Italian immigration shows how newcomers faced struggles, but also enriched American culture.
Just like Chinese immigrants, Italian immigrants helped shape the modern United States.

title: The Value of Time
sentences: Someone once asked me what I considered the most valuable thing in life.
At first, I thought about money, houses, or possessions.
Then I realized that none of those could compare to time.
Time is something that we can never buy back once it is gone.
We often take it for granted, wasting hours on things that do not matter.
But every moment is a gift that we should use wisely.
With time, we can build friendships, learn new skills, and create memories.
Without time, even the richest person would have nothing.
I think about the moments I have shared with my family.
A simple dinner together or a walk in the park is priceless.
These ordinary hours become the foundation of our lives.
Time also teaches us lessons.
It heals our pain, shows us patience, and helps us grow stronger.
That is why I believe time is more valuable than money or possessions.
You can always earn more money, but you cannot create more time.
The best we can do is to spend it with care, and to spend it with people we love.
In the end, when we look back on life, we will not remember the money we made.
We will remember the time we spent, the people we shared it with, and the memories we created.
That is why I try to treasure every day, as if it were my most valuable possession.

title: The Beginning of the Second World War
sentences: In the 1930s, many people in Europe hoped that there would never be another great war.
The memories of the First World War were still painful and fresh.
However, several political events soon destroyed that hope.
After the First World War, Germany had lost much of its power and land.
Many Germans felt angry and humiliated by the peace treaty they were forced to sign.
During the 1930s, a man named Adolf Hitler rose to power in Germany.
He promised to rebuild Germany’s strength and restore its national pride.
Hitler’s government began to rebuild the army and prepare for war.
At first, other European countries tried to avoid conflict.
They believed that by allowing Germany to take small pieces of land, they could prevent another war.
But Hitler’s ambitions continued to grow.
In 1939, Germany invaded Poland.
This time, Britain and France decided that they could not ignore the aggression.
They declared war on Germany, and the Second World War began.
The early years of the war were disastrous for Europe.
German armies moved quickly, conquering many countries.
Millions of soldiers and civilians suffered under the violence and destruction.
In 1941, the war expanded when Germany invaded the Soviet Union.
Later that year, Japan attacked the United States at Pearl Harbor, bringing America into the war.
The conflict had now spread across Europe, Asia, and Africa — it was truly a world war.
The war continued until 1945, leaving behind destruction, suffering, and millions of deaths.
When it finally ended, people around the world hoped that humanity would never make the same mistake again.
The Second World War taught the world a painful lesson — that peace must never be taken for granted.

title: The Story of Summer Festivals
sentences: Every summer, many towns and cities across North America hold special festivals.
These festivals bring people together to celebrate music, art, food, and culture.
Some festivals are small local events, while others attract visitors from all over the country.
Many summer festivals began more than a hundred years ago, just like fall fairs.
In the past, they often marked the end of planting season or celebrated a town’s founding day.
Today, festivals have become an important part of community life.
Music is one of the main attractions of summer festivals.
There are outdoor concerts where people bring chairs and blankets to enjoy live performances.
Country, jazz, rock, and folk music are especially popular during these events.
Food is another big part of summer festivals.
Vendors sell everything from grilled corn and lemonade to international dishes.
Some festivals even focus entirely on food, such as seafood festivals or barbecue competitions.
Many communities also include parades in their festivals.
Colorful floats, marching bands, and dancers fill the streets with energy and excitement.
For children, there are games, face painting, and small amusement rides.
For adults, there may be art shows, local craft markets, and even beer gardens.
Some summer festivals celebrate a specific culture or tradition.
For example, many cities host multicultural festivals where people can learn about different heritages.
Visitors can enjoy traditional music, dances, and foods from around the world.
Festivals also help small businesses and local artists share their work.
Governments and community organizations often support these events because they bring people together.
Like fall fairs, summer festivals are fun for the whole family.
They remind us to celebrate our traditions, enjoy nature, and appreciate the people around us.
Even though cities grow and times change, the spirit of coming together to celebrate never fades.
Summer festivals, just like fall fairs, remain a joyful symbol of North American culture.

title: The Evolution of the Internet
sentences: When the Internet was first created in the late 1960s, it was only used by scientists and researchers.
It was designed as a way for computers to share information across long distances.
At that time, there were no websites, no email, and certainly no social media.
By the 1980s, the Internet had grown larger and began to connect universities and organizations around the world.
In the early 1990s, the invention of the World Wide Web changed everything.
Suddenly, anyone could create a webpage and share information easily.
In the beginning, web pages were simple — mostly text with a few pictures.
As technology improved, websites became more colorful, interactive, and dynamic.
In the late 1990s, email became a popular way for people to communicate.
Soon after, instant messaging and chat rooms appeared, allowing real-time communication.
In the 2000s, the rise of social media changed how people used the Internet.
Websites like Facebook, YouTube, and Twitter allowed users to share their thoughts, photos, and videos instantly.
Smartphones made the Internet even more accessible.
People no longer needed to sit at a desk to go online — they could connect anywhere, anytime.
Modern Internet use goes far beyond communication.
It allows us to shop, study, watch movies, attend meetings, and even control home devices.
Just like the telephone evolved from a simple device into a powerful communication tool,
the Internet has evolved into one of the most essential parts of modern life.
With cloud computing and artificial intelligence, the Internet continues to change rapidly.
People can now store data online, translate languages instantly, and even use virtual assistants to help them work.
But with all these benefits come new challenges, such as privacy, security, and misinformation.
Governments and organizations around the world are working to make the Internet safer and fairer.
The Internet has connected the world in ways that people in the past could never imagine.
As technology keeps advancing, the Internet will surely continue to shape the future of communication.

title: The Rise of the Second Industrial Revolution
sentences: In the late nineteenth century, Europe and North America experienced a great wave of change.
This period is known as the Second Industrial Revolution.
While the first Industrial Revolution had introduced steam power and machinery,
the second one brought electricity, steel, and new forms of transportation.
Cities began to grow quickly as people left farms to work in factories.
Large industries were built to produce goods faster and more efficiently than ever before.
The invention of the electric light bulb changed how people lived and worked.
Factories could now operate both day and night, increasing productivity.
The telephone made communication much faster and easier across long distances.
Railways and steamships connected countries and continents, encouraging global trade.
New industries also emerged, such as chemicals, automobiles, and oil production.
These industries created jobs, but they also caused social and environmental problems.
Workers often faced long hours, low wages, and unsafe working conditions.
Labor unions began to form, demanding better pay and safer workplaces.
Governments started to pass new laws to protect workers and regulate industry.
The spread of public education during this time helped more people learn to read and write.
Newspapers became a powerful way to share news, opinions, and political ideas.
Science also advanced rapidly — discoveries in medicine and physics improved people’s lives.
Yet, industrial progress came at a cost.
The air in large cities was filled with smoke from factories.
Rivers were often polluted by industrial waste.
Despite these problems, people remained optimistic about the future.
They believed that science and technology could solve any challenge.
The Second Industrial Revolution transformed the modern world —
it created the foundations of our current economy, cities, and daily life.
Just like the people of 1914, many believed that progress would continue forever.
But history has taught us that progress also brings responsibility.
To truly move forward, humanity must learn to balance innovation with care for society and the planet.

title: Japanese Immigration to the United States
sentences: During the late nineteenth century, many Japanese people began moving to Hawaii and the United States.
At that time, Japan was changing quickly during the Meiji Restoration.
The country was becoming modern and industrialized, but life was still difficult for many farmers.
There was little land available, and taxes were high.
Many young men decided to seek a better life overseas.
The first group of Japanese immigrants went to Hawaii in 1868 to work on sugar plantations.
They signed contracts to work long hours under the hot sun for very little pay.
The work was hard, but many immigrants stayed after their contracts ended.
Some started small farms, stores, or restaurants, and built communities in Hawaii.
Later, Japanese workers also moved to the western parts of the United States, such as California and Oregon.
They worked on farms, in factories, and on railroads — just like Chinese immigrants before them.
Many Americans, however, did not welcome the Japanese immigrants.
They believed that Japanese workers were taking jobs from local citizens.
In 1907, the U.S. government made an agreement with Japan called the “Gentlemen’s Agreement.”
This agreement stopped most Japanese laborers from coming to the United States,
but allowed the wives and children of those already there to join them.
Despite these restrictions, Japanese communities continued to grow, especially along the West Coast.
Japanese immigrants placed great value on education and hard work.
Their children, born in the U.S., became known as the “Nisei,” meaning “second generation.”
These second-generation Japanese-Americans worked to balance both cultures —
keeping their parents’ traditions while becoming part of American society.
However, during World War II, life changed dramatically for Japanese-Americans.
After Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in 1941, the U.S. government forced over 100,000 Japanese-Americans
to leave their homes and live in internment camps.
Most of these people were innocent citizens who had done nothing wrong.
They lost their homes, businesses, and farms, and many suffered greatly during the war years.
Decades later, the U.S. government formally apologized for this injustice.
Today, Japanese-Americans are an important part of American society.
Their contributions can be seen in business, science, politics, and culture.
From the early plantation workers to modern professionals,
the story of Japanese immigration is one of strength, perseverance, and hope.

title: Tobacco
sentences: Tobacco is one of the oldest plants used by humans for recreation and medicine.
Indigenous peoples in the Americas were the first to grow and use tobacco.
They believed tobacco had spiritual and healing powers.
In the 1500s, European explorers brought tobacco back to Europe.
It quickly became popular, and people began to smoke, chew, or sniff it in many countries.
For centuries, tobacco was considered fashionable and even healthy.
Doctors once recommended smoking to relax the nerves or reduce stress.
However, in the twentieth century, scientists discovered the dangers of tobacco.
They learned that smoking causes serious diseases such as lung cancer, heart disease, and stroke.
Cigarettes contain thousands of chemicals, many of which are toxic.
One of the most dangerous substances in tobacco is nicotine.
Nicotine is an addictive drug that makes it very hard for smokers to quit.
Many smokers start when they are teenagers, often influenced by friends or advertising.
Once addicted, they may continue for years, even knowing the health risks.
In many countries, governments have passed laws to reduce smoking.
Cigarette ads are banned on television, and cigarette packs must carry health warnings.
Smoking is also banned in most public places, such as offices, restaurants, and schools.
Despite these efforts, millions of people around the world still smoke.
Some believe smoking helps them relax or focus, but the feeling is only temporary.
Long-term smoking damages nearly every organ in the body.
Non-smokers can also be harmed by second-hand smoke, which contains the same toxic chemicals.
Many smokers try to quit, but it can be very difficult.
Doctors recommend using nicotine patches, gums, or counseling to help quit smoking.
Public health organizations continue to educate people about the dangers of tobacco.
Today, smoking is no longer seen as glamorous or sophisticated.
Instead, many people see it as a serious health problem that can and should be prevented.
Like alcohol, tobacco is a part of many cultures, but it must be used responsibly — or not at all.

title: Isaac Newton and the Law of Gravity
sentences: Isaac Newton was one of the most important scientists in history.
He was born in England in the year 1643.
As a child, Newton was quiet and enjoyed spending time alone.
He was very curious about how the world worked.
Newton studied mathematics and science at the University of Cambridge.
During this time, he began to think deeply about motion and forces.
One of Newton’s most famous ideas is the law of gravity.
According to legend, Newton began thinking about gravity after seeing an apple fall from a tree.
He wondered why the apple fell straight down instead of moving sideways or upward.
Newton concluded that the earth pulls objects toward its center.
He later realized that this force did not only apply to objects on earth.
The same force that pulls an apple to the ground also controls the motion of the moon and planets.
Newton explained that every object in the universe attracts every other object.
The strength of this attraction depends on the mass of the objects and the distance between them.
Newton also developed important ideas about motion, now called Newton’s laws of motion.
These laws explain how objects move when forces act upon them.
Together, his ideas formed the foundation of classical physics.
For more than two hundred years, scientists used Newton’s laws to understand the universe.
Newton also made important discoveries in optics, the study of light.
He showed that white light is made up of many different colors.
Newton published his ideas in a famous book called *Principia*.
This book changed the way people understood science and nature.
During his lifetime, Newton became highly respected in England.
He was even knighted by the king and became known as Sir Isaac Newton.
Newton died in 1727 and was buried in Westminster Abbey.
Today, Newton is remembered as a scientist who helped humanity understand the laws of nature.
His work shows how careful observation and deep thinking can change the world.

title: The Yangtze River
sentences: The Yangtze River is the longest river in China and the third longest river in the world.
It has played a central role in Chinese history, culture, and economic development for thousands of years.
The river begins in the mountains of western China, on the Tibetan Plateau.
From there, it flows eastward for more than 6,300 kilometers before reaching the East China Sea.
Along its long journey, the Yangtze passes through many different landscapes.
It flows through deep valleys, fertile plains, and some of the most densely populated areas of China.
For centuries, the Yangtze River has been a major transportation route.
Before modern highways and railways existed, boats carried people and goods along the river.
Many important cities grew along the Yangtze because of trade and agriculture.
One of the most famous cities on the river is Shanghai, near its mouth.
Shanghai developed into a major international port and financial center.
Farther inland, cities such as Wuhan and Chongqing also play key roles in industry and transportation.
The Yangtze River has also inspired many poets, painters, and writers.
In traditional Chinese literature, the river often symbolizes life, strength, and continuity.
One of the most famous natural features along the river is the Three Gorges.
These steep cliffs and fast-moving waters were once dangerous for ships.
In modern times, the Three Gorges Dam was built to control flooding and produce electricity.
The dam has provided energy for millions of people, but it has also caused environmental concerns.
Today, the Chinese government works to balance economic development with environmental protection along the river.
Pollution control and wildlife protection have become important goals.
The Yangtze River is home to many unique species, including rare fish and river dolphins.
Although some species are endangered, conservation efforts continue.
For the people living along its banks, the Yangtze is more than just a river.
It provides water, food, transportation, and a sense of cultural identity.
From ancient times to the modern era, the Yangtze River has shaped the life of a nation.
Protecting this great river is essential for the future of China.
